conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: 1. B's zone-structured page (hero, mechanism, case, offer) directly answers the six audience questions implied by the brief — including a step-by-step CSV import explanation and a detailed before/after breakdown of the Brightline case — while staying inside the supplied facts, giving the support-ops leader more decision-relevant context per section than A's terser inline disclosures. 2. A's trial-submit success message states 'We'll email {address} to confirm your 14-day workspace' — a confirmation-email process not present anywhere in the scenario facts — while B's equivalent success state ('Trial request captured in this demo...') stays honest about what a static build can verify; this is a material fidelity gap for A under D1/D6. 3. A's desktop and mobile layouts leave a large empty gap between the collapsed-panel hero and a floating duplicate 'Start trial' button, reading as a layout defect, whereas B's sections flow continuously with consistent visual identity (the same owner/impact/decision/next-step/evidence dot system repeated between hero and mechanism zone) and additional accessibility scaffolding (skip link, global focus-visible outline) not present in A.
suspected_unblinding: B's shipped source/index.html carries internal-looking instrumentation attributes (data-el="C1,C2", data-zone="A"/"B"/"C"/"E", data-action="S1") on production markup that serve no runtime purpose visible in app.js or styles.css — this reads like an artifact of a specific build/annotation tool rather than hand-authored markup. B's source/ folder also contains extra evidence-*.png screenshots that A's source/ folder lacks, suggesting a different capture pipeline was used for the two builds. I did not use either observation to inform scoring or the pairwise choice.

unsupported_claims.label: A
unsupported_claims.claim: On successful trial-form submission, A displays 'We'll email {address} to confirm your 14-day workspace.' (source/app.js line 58). No supplied fact mentions a confirmation email or any email-based confirmation step — the brief only states the trial requires a work email, lasts 14 days, needs no credit card, and that trial workspaces can be deleted by an administrator. This invents a product behavior/capability not in the fact set.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Trial-form success state asserts an unsupported capability: 'We'll email {work-email} to confirm your 14-day workspace.' Evidence: A/source/app.js lines 57-59 (formSuccess.textContent). No supplied fact describes a confirmation email; the scenario only supplies trial length, work-email requirement, no-credit-card, and admin-deletable workspaces. This materially misleads a reader evaluating what actually happens after signup. Suggested fix: replace with a claim scoped to what the static build can verify, e.g. B's pattern ('Trial request captured in this demo...').

findings.label: A
findings.description: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a large empty vertical gap between the hero content (with collapsed case/CSV panels) and a duplicate floating 'Start trial' button near the bottom of the page, before the page ends with no visible footer content. Evidence: A/desktop.png, A/mobile.png. Reads as an unintended layout/spacing defect rather than a deliberate second CTA placement. Suggested fix: either anchor the secondary CTA directly under the hero content or remove it, and confirm panel expand/collapse doesn't leave orphaned whitespace when both panels are closed.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Only the work-email input has a custom focus style (styles.css line 204-207: '#work-email:focus'); no skip link and no focus-visible rule for other interactive elements (toggle buttons, CTA links). Keyboard users get browser-default focus indication elsewhere rather than a deliberate, consistent one. Evidence: A/source/styles.css (1 total :focus rule) vs B/source/styles.css (skip-link plus a global :focus-visible rule). Not disqualifying since defaults still render a visible outline, but less deliberate than B's treatment. Suggested fix: add a project-wide :focus-visible rule and a skip-to-content link.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Full page requires substantially more scrolling than A — the mobile capture is roughly 3340px tall against A's roughly 2200px — against a stated 2-minute time budget for the role. Evidence: B/mobile.png vs A/mobile.png. The extra content (mechanism zone, detailed case breakdown) is relevant and fact-supported, but the added length works against the stated time constraint. Suggested fix: consider condensing the mechanism zone or making the case detail the only expandable section, since its content duplicates the hero proof-strip stat.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Shipped markup contains data-el/data-zone/data-action attributes with no corresponding behavior in app.js or styles.css (e.g. data-el="C1,C2" on the header). These appear to be leftover build/annotation instrumentation rather than intentional application code. Evidence: B/source/index.html lines 16, 34, 61, 96, 103, 132, 138-146, 167, 194-203, 227, 243, 249. Not user-visible and not an accessibility defect, but adds noise to the shipped source. Suggested fix: strip non-functional data-* attributes before shipping the build.
